messages:
alex: Hey — running into a weird one on Windows 11. `redwoodctl login --profile=staging` seems to succeed but the CLI later uses the default profile when I run `redwoodctl invoke`. Any ideas?

maria: hmm, do you see multiple config files? what's `redwoodctl --version` and `redwoodctl config path` show?

alex: redwoodctl 0.8.1
redwoodctl config path -> C:\\Users\\alex\\.redwood\\config.json
redwoodctl cache path -> C:\\Users\\alex\\AppData\\Roaming\\Redwood\\cache.json
I ran `redwoodctl login --profile=staging --debug` and it printed `auth: saved token to C:\\Users\\alex\\.redwood\\config.json (profile: staging)` but `redwoodctl whoami` shows user in `default` profile.

maria: can you paste the `--debug` snippet where it writes the file? sometimes backslashes get doubled in logs and the parser fails to load the profile.

alex: paste below:
```
[debug] saving config to C:\\Users\\alex\\.redwood\\config.json
[debug] profile key: staging
[info] login succeeded, token cached
```

maria: ok. two possibilities: 1) the CLI writes the config to a different logical path for reads (we had a bug where config loader used %USERPROFILE% while writer used %HOMEDRIVE%%HOMEPATH%), or 2) the token is being cached to AppData and the invoker picks from cache by default unless profile env var present.

kevin: cc @maria i'm pretty sure we had a Windows path normalization fix in the runtime but maybe not in the config codepath. PR 402 fixed backslash normalization for model cache paths — similar area. i can look.

sam: quick workaround: `set REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging` in your shell or pass `--profile staging` to every command. Not ideal but unblocks you.

alex: setting REDWOOD_PROFILE works, thx. Would still like to fix so onboarding CLI flow works for new hires on Windows.

maria: can you test this patch locally? run `pip install -e .` from cli/ and then run `redwoodctl login --profile=staging && redwoodctl whoami`

alex: tried the local build — login writes the profile now but `redwoodctl invoke` still picks default unless i restart the shell. maybe env cache in background process?

dev-bot: token-refresh-service: refreshed token for default profile at 1758201302

alex: aha — the token-refresh-service (desktop helper) is still writing to the global cache and overwriting the active profile token. looks like background refresher only uses `default` when REDWOOD_PROFILE not explicitly set.

maria: that explains it. filing a bug: background refresher should pick the profile of the originating login session or namespaced cache per profile.

kevin: created issue #789: "background auth refresher ignores profile on Windows" and a draft fix to write per-profile cache files (cache-{profile}.json) + normalize paths. PR coming.

sam: FYI — documentation note: onboarding steps should include `setx REDWOOD_PROFILE staging` for Windows until the fix lands. adding to docs/quickstart.

alex: leaving this here for anyone else: workaround commands that helped me:
```
redwoodctl login --profile staging
set REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging
taskkill /IM redwood-token-refresher.exe /F || echo no background refresher
redwoodctl whoami
```

maria: thanks. i merged a small change to treat backslashes and to prefer cache-{profile}.json when present on Windows. will monitor. :thumbsup:

kevin: PR #810 merged to main; will be included in 0.8.2.

alex: confirmed on 0.8.2-beta — login + invoke now honor `--profile` without needing env var. closing my local workaround. thanks team! :tada:

sam: i'll update onboarding doc and the 'windows gotchas' section in devex.

maria: leaving this thread open for a couple days in case regressions pop up.

alex: sounds good — marking resolved for me.
